paper.title: llama.cpp b12674
paper.abstract: opencl: fetch the Adreno binary kernel library at configure time for Windows on Snapdragon ( #31759 ) opencl: fetch the Adreno binary kernel library at configure time Make GGML_OPENCL_USE_ADRENO_BIN_KERNELS an option, default ON, and add GGML_OPENCL_ADRENO_BIN_KERNELS_FETCH, default ON. On Windows, CMake downloads the pinned adreno-opencl-kernels release from the Qualcomm Software Center, verifies its SHA256, and copies the DLL and its license next to the executables. A failed download is only a warning; the backend then uses its builtin kernels. The opencl-adreno release job turns the fetch off, since it ships only ggml-opencl.dll. opencl: fetch the Adreno binary kernel library only on ARM64 The library is built for Windows on ARM64 only. opencl: add download timeout and better handle output dir Assisted-by: Codex opencl: add .txt to license file Assisted-by: Codex Co-authored-by: Li He lih@qti.qualcomm.com Website: https://llama.app Attestations: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/71506489 macOS/iOS: macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED macOS Intel (x64) iOS XCFramework Linux: Ubuntu x64 (CPU) Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) Ubuntu 24.04 s390x (CPU) Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide Android: Android arm64 (CPU) Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide Windows: Windows x64 (CPU) Windows arm64 (CPU) Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs Windows x64 (Vulkan) Windows arm64 (Vulkan) Windows x64 (OpenVINO) Windows x64 (SYCL) Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) openEuler: DISABLED openEuler x86 (310p) openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) openEuler aarch64 (310p) openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) UI: UI

paper.title: llama.cpp b12671
paper.abstract: metal : batch concat rows and copy them in vector chunks ( #32824 ) metal : batch concat rows and copy them in vector chunks The concat kernel copied one element per thread, so wide rows with many rows ran at a fraction of the memory bandwidth. Batch several rows per threadgroup and copy the contiguous dim-0 elements in 4-element chunks when the row is contiguous. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) test : cover concat vector and misaligned row paths Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) metal : hoist the concat src1 row offset into scalars Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) metal : peel to align the concat vector copy Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) metal : vectorize concat rows along any dimension Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) metal : specialize concat with function constants Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) metal : drop the concat row-batch dispatch Batching several rows per threadgroup reduces the number of threads by the batch factor. On machines with a large GPU this leaves too few requests in flight and the copy becomes latency bound: M5 Ultra (36 CPU) f16 [1024,8,256,1] d=0 8.1 us -> 17.2 us f32 [4096,8,256,1] d=0 35.4 us -> 118.5 us f16 [4096,8,256,1] d=2 50.9 us -> 102.0 us An interleaved sweep of the (nth, nrptg) dispatch over the concat perf cases on an M2 Ultra and an M5 Ultra shows that the base dispatch is best or tied for every shape once the rows are vectorized, and that the gains of the previous commit come from the vector copy alone: M2 Ultra f16 [1024,8,256,1] d=0 32.4 us -> 17.0 us M5 Ultra f16 [1024,8,256,1] d=0 13.3 us -> 8.1 us Keep the vector copy and the function-constant specialization, and return to the original dispatch. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) metal : revert the concat function constants Specializing the concat kernel on the concat dimension and on whether a row is split across threadgroups with function constants makes the strided scalar path slower. Interleaved over the concat perf cases on an M5 Ultra, the specialized kernel is not faster than the plain one, and it costs up to 18% on shapes that are already at the memory bandwidth limit: f32 [2050,8,256,1] b=255 d=0 21.0 us -> 25.1 us f32 [2050,8,256,1] b=256 d=2 31.1 us -> 36.7 us f16 [4096,8,256,1] b=256 d=2 31.2 us -> 36.7 us Revert the specialization and keep copying rows with the runtime arguments. The concat change is now limited to the kernel itself. paper.title: llama.cpp b12668
paper.abstract: metal : support BF16/F32 src1 for MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID ( #32677 ) llama, metal : support BF16 src1 for MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID Add GGML_PREC_BF16 handling for src1 on the Metal backend when the tensor API is available: MUL_MAT with an F32 src0 stages the A tile as bfloat, and MUL_MAT_ID stages src1 as bfloat instead of F16. The tensor path keeps src1 in F32 when it reads the operand directly. Add a temporary LLAMA_MOE_AMAX_SKIP env var that disables the graph-level amax rescaling for the MoE down projection and sets the BF16 src1 hint instead. Apply the hint inside build_lora_mm_id so it reaches the matmul before the per-expert scale and LoRA nodes wrap it. Add MUL_MAT_ID src1 BF16 test cases to test-backend-ops. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) metal : support BF16 src1 without the tensor API Allow GGML_PREC_BF16 when the device has bfloat, not only when it has the Metal4 tensor API. Add legacy _prec_bf16 kernels for MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID that stage src1 as bfloat in the threadgroup and run the simdgroup multiply with bfloat A and B. The F16 MUL_MAT_ID kernel uses half A on the tensor path and bfloat A on the legacy path. Cast the quantized dequantize outputs to the destination element type: the older Metal compiler on M2 rejects implicit float to bfloat. Tested on M2 Ultra (legacy): MUL_MAT_PREC_SRC1 24/24 and MUL_MAT_ID_PREC_SRC1_BF16 30/30. Flint Q4_K_M with LLAMA_MOE_AMAX_SKIP=1: pp512 -2.1%, tg128 +25.5% vs master. On M5 Max: pp512 +2.1%, tg128 +22.2%. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) metal : derive matrix types with value_type helpers Add value_type_4x4/value_type_2x4/value_type_8x8 helpers and use them in the MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID kernels so the templates take only the underlying types and derive the matrix types. Add TODOs for the remaining kernels. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) metal : derive matrix types in the remaining kernels Use the value_type_* helpers in the flash-attention, top-k-mask, mul-mv and count-equal kernels to derive the matrix/vector types from the underlying scalar types, and simplify the FA_TYPES macros. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) metal : enable BF16 in the tensor API metallib The tensor API requires macOS 26, where bfloat is always available, so define GGML_METAL_HAS_BF16 when compiling the tensor metallib. This makes the bfloat specializations of the value_type helpers visible to fa_tensor.metal and includes the prec_bf16 kernels in the prebuilt tensor metallib. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) metal : support GGML_PREC_F32 for src1 in MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID Split the tensor-API and legacy simdgroup mul_mm/mul_mm_id kernels into separate files and library kinds, following the fa_tensor.metal example. The legacy kernels, including the new _prec_f32 variants that stage src0 and src1 as float in shared memory, are compiled into the default mul_mm library; the tensor variants live in a separate mul_mm_tensor library kind and carry a _tensor host-name infix. Tensor devices run F32 src1 matmuls on the simdgroup path instead of the tensor API, which rounds float operands to a reduced precision. This removes the MUL_MM_SG kind and the #undef GGML_METAL_HAS_TENSOR compile. Add MUL_MAT_ID_PREC_SRC1_F32 tests. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) cont : indentation llama : move the MoE amax skip into the precision policy Add llm_arch_mmid_down_bf16() for the architectures whose MoE down projection uses the graph-level amax rescaling. Extract the precision policy setup from load_tensors() into llama_model_base::load_prec_policy(), and move the LLAMA_MOE_AMAX_SKIP handling there: it sets prec_src1 = BF16 for ffn_down_exps before the per-tensor policy is loaded. build_moe_ffn() now skips the amax rescaling when the policy requests BF16. Apply the policy with the original weight so cached experts get it, drop the prec_src1 parameter from build_lora_mm_id(), and remove the prec_src1 serialization from the model saver. paper.abstract: Patch release v5.24.1 A patch to fix a bunch of stuff for vLLM, a few distributed issues, and some model fixes (llama4, dory); see the full list vLLM related Fix backward compatibility of the cache rename for remote code ( #51085 ) by @hmellor Restore modeling_attn_mask_utils for remote code (one-off to unblock vLLM) ( #51124 ) by @hmellor Expose past_key_values in MBartDecoderLayer.forward signature for remote code ( #51177 ) by @hmellor [OmniASR] Support a padding_mask kept on the CPU in the audio encoder ( #51100 ) by @El-euchidali Model fixes Fix Llama4 forward crash on missing image_outputs ( #51144 ) by @kylesayrs Fix dory static cache ( #50993 ) by @ArthurZucker Distributed Allow expert parallelism alone with tp_plan={} ( #50996 ) by @3outeille Fix strided checkpoint reads on PyTorch 2.9 ( #51042 ) by @satsuki2486441738 Full Changelog : v5.24.0...v5.24.1
